prompt: What kind of call is this?

options.text: Banking, account, or payment
options.legit_contrast: A real bank may call about suspicious activity, but it moves money only between the customer's own accounts, never asks for a full PIN or one-time code, and is happy for the customer to hang up and call the number on their card.

questions.prompt: Who does the caller say they are?

options.text: A bank fraud or security team

Not stated

questions.note: Every option scores zero. This attribute is recorded because it is what makes the call an impersonation, and because the verdict has to be explainable to the person: 'someone claiming to be your bank asked you to move money'. It is not scored, because a real bank also says it is a bank, so on its own it separates nothing.

scoring.formula: score = sum of the value of every chosen option
scoring.verdict: above the scam cut-off means scam, below the legitimate cut-off means a real call, in between means the call gave nothing to go on
scoring.note: There are no question weights. Every question counts the same, so the strength of a signal is expressed in the option values themselves: a strong indicator uses 1.0, a weaker one a smaller number. Questions marked role 'recorded' score zero on every option; they are captured for the explanation, not for the verdict.
scoring.thresholds_are_configurable: RQ2 moves the scam cut-off per user profile. The default of zero makes the verdict the sign of the sum.
scoring.known_limitation: A plain sum treats every attribute as independent, so it cannot express a combination such as 'claims to be a bank AND asks for payment in gift cards', which is far more suspicious than either answer alone. Capturing such interactions is left as future work; the attributes involved are recorded so that it remains possible.
